messages:
Elena Park: Quick design question for the marketplace launch: how should we handle multi-SI claim conflicts when two integrators claim leads for the same account? Need deterministic rules before we build the automation.

Noah Reed: Good catch. Real-world cases: 1) duplicate signups (different emails) 2) same corporate account but different org units 3) partner referral + marketplace inbound. We should have a conflict matrix.

Zara Malik: Proposal (short): priority order = (explicit partner referral) > (partner claimed via portal first) > (higher trial_activity_score). Add manual override by Redwood AE.

Luis Ortega: +1. Suggest we add a tie-breaker: earliest partner_claimed_at wins. If both claim within 1h and equal activity score -> escalate to partnership inbox for human triage.

Elena Park: Nice. Can we express that as simple rules we can implement in SFDC flows / partner dashboard? Pseudocode would help.

Noah Reed: Pseudocode draft:
```
on lead created or partner claim event:
  if lead.referral_partner != null:
    assign owner = referral_partner
  else if multiple_claims:
    sort claims by claimed_at asc
    pick top_claim
    if time_between(top_claim, second_claim) <= 1h:
      if top_claim.activity_score == second_claim.activity_score:
        create triage_task -> partnerships@redwood.ai
      else:
        assign owner = claim with higher activity_score
    else:
      assign owner = top_claim
  else:
    assign owner = first_claim
```

Zara Malik: We'll need fields: lead_source, referral_partner_id, claims[] (partner_id, claimed_at, activity_score), assigned_partner_id, auto_escalate_flag, triage_ticket_url. We'll capture claims as partner_claim records linked to lead.

Luis Ortega: For CRM exports and partner CSVs keep flat fields for easy consumption: account_id, company_name, lead_source, assigned_partner_id, partner_claim_ts, partner_activity_score, triage_flag, reassign_reason. That avoids nested arrays for downstream finance/ops.

PartnerOps Bot: Draft playbook page created: https://confluence.redwood.ai/partners/si-claim-conflict-matrix (editable) and Jira PART-15233 created (assignee: Noah Reed) - https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/PART-15233

Elena Park: Owners? Noah - own SFDC flow + tie-breaker logic. Zara - update playbook + examples. Luis - CSV schema + dashboard alerts. I'll coordinate with Legal for consent language re: partner referrals.

Noah Reed: I can own SFDC flow. Will post the flow spec and edge-case unit tests in the Jira.

Zara Malik: I'll add 3 examples to the playbook (duplicate emails, multi-org, referral override) and include the pseudo-code + screenshots.

Luis Ortega: Adding CSV schema to playbook now and will wire alerts (triage queue SLA 8h).

Elena Park: One more: define "activity_score" formula so partners and Redwood agree. Suggest: activity_score = 0.5*trial_usage_pct + 0.3*engagement_events + 0.2*days_since_signup_norm. Thoughts?

Noah Reed: Good start. Keep it simple initially: activity_score = (trial_usage_pct * 0.6) + (recent_logins_last_7d * 0.4). We can iterate. Document versioning in playbook.

Zara Malik: I'll add the scoring formula and a note that scoring is configurable per partner or per listing.

PartnerOps Bot: Reminder: Playbook review meeting scheduled Thu 9am PT. Invite sent.

Elena Park: Thanks team. Once playbook + SFDC flow + CSV schema are in place we'll schedule a partner sign-off call. :white_check_mark:
